 Judgment
The petitioner has filed this petition U/s 22 of the Employee's Compensation Act, claiming compensation, for the injury sustained by him during the course of his employment under the respondent.

The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 02.03.2021 at about 10.30  11.00 a.m., the petitioner was operating the machine during the course of duty accidentally his right hand was caught in between the lathe machine, as a result he sustained grievous injuries on his right hand.

Immediately after the incident, the petitioner was shifted to St.Martha's Hospital, Bengaluru and thereafter he was admitted to SCCH4 3 ECA No.62/2021 Hosmat Hospital where he was still under treatment and he has spent Rs.50,000/ towards his medical,
conveyance and other expenses.
3. Prior to the accident, petitioner was very hale and healthy working as Lathe Machine Operator under respondent and he was drawing salary of Rs.18,000/ p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to continue his work and is under complete bed rest and he is suffering from permanent disability.
The respondent is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hence,
prays to award compensation of Rs.15,00,000/ with interest.

4. After service of notice the respondent has appeared through his counsel and filed written statement contending that, the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed in limine.

The petitioner has joined for the job with the SCCH4 4 ECA No.62/2021 respondent only on 27.02.2021 and not as averred that he was working with the respondent since three years which is nothing but a wet lie.
The petitioner negligently switched on the lathe machine by keeping his right hand on the lathe machine check.
Suddenly the machine started and the petitioner's right hand got struck inside the Lathe Machine Check resulting in the said injuries to his right hand.
The incident was completely witnessed by the other employees by Name Arzoo and Subramani who were on the other machines.
On witnessing the Arzoo Subramani immediately came for rescue and Subramani Switched off the Lathe and Arzoo tried to stop further mishap by pulling the hand of the petitioner.

The said Arzoo and Subramani smelt liquor smell from the petitioner's mouth, but Arzoo did not express anything and immediately called the respondent over phone and told about the incident what had happened in the factory.
Consequently the respondent asked Arzoo to immediately SCCH4 5 ECA No.62/2021 take the petitioner to the hospital.
The petitioner took the private hospitals but two hospitals whey they came near petitioner to inspect they smelt drunken smell from the petitioner and refused to admit him to the hospital.
Consequently the petitioner was taken to St.Martha's Hospital, Bengaluru wherein he was admitted as an inpatient and he underwent surgery for the injuries sustained.

The petitioner went to post operative dressing accompanied by Arzoo every 5 days once and the respondent used to give Rs.4,000/ for petitioner every time which went on for 5 weeks and the went 6 time to Marth's Hospital along with Arzoo.
The accident might have occurred during the course of employment but the accident has occurred under the influence of alcohol.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner.
The compensation has claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, the SCCH4 6 ECA No.62/2021 respondent No.1 have prays to dismiss the petition with cost.

5. On the basis of rival contention, the following issues are framed :

2
1. Whether the petitioner proves that he was "employee" under the respondent?
2. Whether petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injury during the course of employment under the re spondent?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so how much and from whom?
4. What Order?
6. The petitioner, in order to prove his claim petition, got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 10 and 17.
Two witnesses is examined as PW.2 and 3, through them got marked Ex.P11 to 16.
The respondent examined himself as RW.1, SCCH4 7 ECA No.62/2021 through him got marked documents at Ex.R.1 to 16.
One witness by name M.D.Danish Ikbal @ Arzoo is examined as RW.2, his signature is marked Ex.R.6 (a) to (c).
7. I have heard the arguments of counsel for both the parties.
8. My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1 : In the affirmative,
 Issue No.2 :

In the affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the affirmative,
 Issue No.4 : As per the final orders  for the following:

: R E A S O N S:
ISSUE NO.1 & 2 : Since these two issues are interconnected they are taken up together for common discussion to avoid repetition of the facts.
9.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed his affidavit in lieu of chiefexamination, which is considered as P.W.1.

In SCCH4 8 ECA No.62/2021 support of his case, he has produced certified copies of acknowledgement issued by the police, police intimation letter, complaint lodged to police, wound certificate and discharge summary,which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 5.
10.

As per the documents, the petitioner has lodged complaint with Magadi Police, on 05.07.2021 alleging that, on 02.03.2021, while he was working as lathe machine Operator in Shivashakthi Engineering Works, Gubbanna Industrial Area, 6th Block, Rajajinagar, Bengaluru, at about 11.00 p.m., the right hand finger caught to the lathe machine and small finger was cut.

sentences.text: Since the factory owner Srinivas i.e., respondent herein did not take any precautionary measure.
11. Upon receiving the complaint, the police have issued acknowledgement but FIR is not registered.

As per the wound certificate issued by St.Martha's Hospital, Bengaluru, the petitioner has taken E.Purushotham vs Srinivasan.P on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86859105/
3 treatment on SCCH4 9 ECA No.62/2021 02.03.2021 i.e., on the date of alleged incident.

sentences.text: IN the wound certificate it is mentioned that, petitioner sustained injuries in working place.
As per the wound certificate the petitioner sustained five injuries.

As per the discharge summary issued by the St.Martha's hospital, the petitioner was admitted as an inpatient from 02.03.2021 to 05.03.2021 it is mentioned that, right hand 3rd finger, amputation of the pulp of the 1st and 5th finger, Mallet finger deformity of 4th finger.
Raw area over dorsum of hand.
The petitioner has also produced three photographs and CD of the photos at Ex.P.8.
In the photos also it is seen middle finer is fully amputed and 5th finger is amputed for half.
12. The respondent himself got examined as RW.1.

In the written statement as well as examination in chief this respondent has contended that, the petitioner had joined for the job in the factory of respondent only on SCCH4 10 ECA No.62/2021 27.02.2021, the petitioner negligently switched on the lathe machine by keeping his right hand on the late machine check.
Suddenly the machine started and the petitioner right hand got struck inside the lathe machine check resulting in the said injuries his right hand.

The RW.1 has produced the medical bills, discharge summary, police intimation, true copy of first information statement, endorsement issued by Magadi road police, 3 vouchers, copy of registration certificate, copy of ESI registration, 4 qualification certificate of employees who are employed in the respondent company, employees salary bank account,
attendance certificate, monthly status report to show that the petitioner was working earlier at GPM solutions till Feb15th 2021, lathe machine installed in our factor along with preventive maintenance certificate, employee ID, ISO registration certificate and 2 photos of petitioner wherein at present is working which are marked at Ex.P.1 to 16.
SCCH4 11 ECA No.62/2021 13.
M.D.Danish Ikbal @ Arzoo who is working in the respondent factory is examined as RW.2, his signatures is marked at Ex.R.6 is marked as Ex.R.6(a) to (c).
This witness has deposed that, he used to take the petitioner for post operative dressing every five days once.
For post operative dressing and treatment of the petitioner was supposed to go Hospital every five days once and respondent used to give Rs.4,000/ every time.
Accordingly, the RW.2 was accompanying the petitioner to the hospital on 5 times.
14. It is undisputed fact that petitioner sustained injury, while he was working in factory of respondent.
There was negligence on the part of the petitioner himself.

4
3. After the incident the respondent has spent Rs.1,40,000/ for the medical treatment of the petitioner.
4. The petitioner was under influence of alcohol .

Hence, I intent to refer the provisions of Section 2 of Employees Compensation Act, which reads as fallows:
(dd)"employee" means a person, who is (i) a railway servant as defined in clause (34) of section 2 of the Railways Act, 1989 (24 of 1989), not permanently employed in any administrative district or sub divisional office of a railway and not employed in any such capacity as is specified in Schedule II; or (ii) (a) a master, seaman or other members of the crew of a ship, (b) a captain or other member of the crew of an aircraft, (c) a person recruited as driver, helper,
SCCH4 13 ECA No.62/2021 mechanic, cleaner or in any other capacity in connection with a motor vehicle, (d) a person recruited for work abroad by a company, and who is employed outside India in any such capacity as is specified in Schedule II and the ship, aircraft or motor vehicle, or company, as the case may be, is registered in India; or (iii) employed in any such capacity as is specified in Schedule II, whether the contract of employment was made before or after the passing of this Act and whether such contract is expressed or implied, oral or in writing;
but does not include any person working in the capacity of a member of the Armed Forces of the Union; and any reference to any employee who has been injured shall, where the employee is dead,
include a reference to his dependants or any of them; (e) "employer" includes any body of persons whether incorporated or not and any managing agent of an employer and the legal SCCH4 14 ECA No.62/2021 representative of a deceased employer, and, when the services of an employee are temporarily lent or let on hire to another person by the person with whom the employee has entered into a contract of service or apprenticeship, means such other person while the employee is working for him; "
15.
This above provision does not make difference between permanent and temporary employee.

16. Section 3 of Employees' compensation Act reads as fallows:
Employer's liability for compensation.--
(1) If personal injury is caused to an employee by accident arising out of and in the course of his employment, his employer shall be liable to pay compensation in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter:Provided that the employer shall not E.Purushotham vs Srinivasan.P on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86859105/
5 be so liable (a) in respect of any injury which does not result in the total or partial disablement of the employee for a period exceeding three days; (b) in respect of any injury, not SCCH4 15 ECA No.62/2021 resulting in death or permanent total disablement caused by an accident which is directly attributable to (i) the employee having been at the time thereof under the influence of drink or drugs, or (ii) the willful disobedience of the employee to an order expressly given, or to a rule expressly framed, for the purpose of securing the safety of employees, or (iii) the willful removal or disregard by the employee of any safety guard or other device which he knew to have been provided for the purpose of securing the safety of employee.
17. As per the above provision the respondent has to prove the willful negligence of the petitioner.
But the respondent has not taken the defence of willful negligence of the petitioner.
That even otherwise there is no material evidence on record to prove the willful negligence or mere negligence of the petitioner.
Though the respondent has contended that petitioner was consumed alcohol, but is not proved medically.

During the course of arguments the learned counsel appearing for petitioner has relied on Judgment the Hon'bel High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.1247/2016 in the case of Superintendent Engineer V/s Smt.D.L.Kavitha and others.

entities.text: Superintendent Engineer V/s Smt.D.L.Kavitha and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this said Judgment, while dealing with the claim petition under the provisions of Employee of Compensation Act, by relying upon the Judgment of Hon'ble High Court it is also held that, while dealing with claim petition under section of 166 of MV Act when the similar contention was raised, held that, deduction cannot be allowed from the amount of compensation either on account of insurance or on account of pensionary benefits or gratuity benefit on account of employment to a kin of the deceased.
19. Explanation to section 4 (2)(b) of the Employee's compensation Act says that.

Any payment or SCCH4 17 ECA No.62/2021 allowance which the [employee] has received from the employer towards his medical treatment shall not be deemed to be a payment or allowance received by him by way of compensation within the meaning of clause (a) of the proviso".
20.
In view of the above provision and citation the defence set out by the respondent is not acceptable.
21. As per settled principle of law the standard of proof in claim petition like the present one is only probabilities of preponderance.

There are no reasons to discard the evidence of petitioner All the E.Purushotham vs Srinivasan.P on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86859105/
6 materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the incident took place on 02.03.2021 at about 10.30 a.m., to 11.00 a.m., while he was working under the respondent.
There was employee and employer relationship between the petitioner and SCCH4 18 ECA No.62/2021 respondent.
Accordingly, I answer issues No.1 & 2 in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
22.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries while he was working under the respondent.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.

23. The petitioner, to prove his disability has examined Dr.B.Ramesh, Orthopedic Surgeon Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru is examined as PW.2, through him OPD card and xray are produced at Ex.P.11 and 12.

This witness has deposed that, the petitioner sustained of right hand with amputation of 3rd finger amputation of pulp of 1st and 5th finger, deformity of 4th finger, fracture of phalanges of 1st and 4th finer and 2nd metacarpal and the petitioner has taken treatment of debridement, K wire fixation of 1, 2, 4th finger and flap cover, later 'K' SCCH4 19 ECA No.62/2021 wires removed.
PW.2 has deposed that, the petitioner has sustained 40% of right upper limb which is 14% of whole body.

24. The petitioner has also examined, Dr.R.Shashikanth, Senior Medical Officer at St.Martha's Hospital, Bengaluru is examined as PW.3, through him OPD card, MLC extract, police intimation letter and inpatient record which are marked at Ex.P.13 to 16.
This witness has deposed for having treated the petitioner for the injuries mentioned in the wound certificate and discharge summary.
25. Though the PW.2 deposed 14% disability but as per schedule No.1 of the Employee's Compensation Act,the divisibility to loss of a finger is 14% to whole body and injury to phalanges is 11%.
The disability provided in the Act prevails over the oral evidence of SCCH4 20 ECA No.62/2021 PW.2.
Hence I hold that, petitioner totally sustained permanent avocational disability at 25%.
26. As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P.5 the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient for a period of 4 days.
According to the petitioner he was earning Rs.18,000/ including over time per month.
But as per Ex.P.18 bank statement it is seen that, the petitioner was getting salary of Rs.14,669/ per month.
27. The petitioner has also produced 12 medical bills which are marked at Ex.P.10, amounting to Rs.5,294/.
These documents are not disproved by the respondent and there is also no reasons to disbelieve the medical bills.
Hence the petitioner is entitle for medical expenses.
28. The petitioner has produced his aadhar card marked under Ex.P.9, as per these documents the date of birth of the year of the petitioner is mentioned 1977.
The SCCH4 21 ECA No.62/2021 accident was occurred in the year2021.

So, as on the date of the accident the petitioner was aged 44 E.Purushotham vs Srinivasan.P on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86859105/
7 years.
As per schedule 4 of the Act the factor applicable to the age of the petitioner is 172.52.

Hence, I inclined to award the future loss of income based on 60% of the proved income (Rs.8,801/ X 25%=Rs.2,200/), Rs.2,200/ X 172.52 =Rs.3,79,544/ which is the total loss of future income plus medical expenses of Rs. Rs.5,294/ in all Rs.3,84,838/.
31.
The respondent being the employer is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner with interest at the rate of 12% p.a., Accordingly, I answer issue No.3 partly in the affirmative.
SCCH4 23 ECA No.62/2021

ISSUE NO.4:
32.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner under section 22 of Employees Compensation Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of Rs. 3,84,838/ (Rupees three lakh eighty four thousand eight hundred and thirty eight Only) with interest at the rate of 12% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondent.
The respondent is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.

8
Considering the quantum of amount awarded to the petitioner it is order to release the entire amount.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/.
Draw up award accordingly.
